item.title: Venezuela cracked. Will Cuba follow?
item.description: The lights are going out in Cuba. Commercial flights into Havana can no longer refuel at the international airport. The capital's bus network has largely ground to a halt. Trash is piling up on the streets, with most collection trucks sitting idle for lack of diesel. Many embassies are closing or drawing down staff. More than half the island’s electric grid is offline. item.title: The man at the center of the Board of Peace
item.description: Argentina, Armenia, Belarus, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Pakistan, Paraguay, Vietnam – to name only a few.The eclectic group could pass for the roster of a niche Olympic sport. In fact, it is part of the membership roll of US President Donald Trump’s newly-minted Board of Peace, which meets today for the first time in Washington, D.C. item.title: NATO, Trump, and Europe’s wake-up call with Ivo Daalder
item.description: Listen: At the Munich Security Conference, European leaders signaled a quiet but unmistakable message: they are ready to move forward, even as Washington’s role grows uncertain. Former US Ambassador to NATO Ivo Daalder explains why this moment represents a permanent rebalancing of responsibilities, after a long-standing reliance on the US for defense. “No, it’s not going to be the same as it’s been in the past decades,” he says. “That’s gone.”The conversation explores the Russian threat looming
